climate.overview_html: The 2026 Global Carbon Budget — released today in Earth System Science Data alongside a companion Nature Climate Change paper — projects global fossil CO2 will fall 0.4% to 38.2 billion tonnes in 2026, the first annual decline since the COVID-era drop of 2020; but rising land-use emissions (Southeast Asian peat fires fuelled by El Niño) push total CO2 to a record 43.3 billion tonnes, leaving only ~150 billion tonnes before the 1.5°C budget is exhausted. The finding arrives on Day 2 of COP31 in Antalya, where a finance clash immediately erupted, with the EU declaring new financing pledges “dead in the water” as Turkey promoted a non-binding electrification pledge that drew pushback for lacking a clean-energy qualifier. The November 3 US midterms produced a Democratic sweep of both chambers, reopening the possibility of congressional investigation into IRA fund redirections, though the One Big Beautiful Bill’s gutting of residential clean-energy credits remains law.

items.headline: Global Carbon Budget 2026: Fossil CO<sub>2</sub> Falls 0.4% to 38.2 Gt — First Decline Since COVID — But Total Emissions Hit Record 43.3 Gt as SE Asian Peat Fires Surge; ~150 Gt Budget Remaining to 1.5°C
items.summary: The Global Carbon Project's 2026 annual budget, published November 10 in Earth System Science Data (preprint essd-2026-895) alongside a companion paper in Nature Climate Change, projects global fossil CO₂ emissions to fall 0.4% to 38.2 billion tonnes in 2026 — the first year-on-year decline since 2020. The decline is driven by the Iran conflict's oil-demand shock (oil −1.9%), solar and wind capacity displacing thermal generation, and China's coal/oil pullback (China overall −0.9%; oil use −5%). Counterweights: coal +0.6%, gas −0.3%, India +4.4% driven by coal. Land-use change emissions surge to 5.1 billion tonnes driven by peat fires in Sumatra and Kalimantan amplified by El Niño, pushing total CO₂ to a record 43.3 billion tonnes (vs. 42.8 Gt in 2025). Atmospheric CO₂ reaches 427.7 ppm, 54% above pre-industrial levels. The remaining carbon budget consistent with limiting warming to 1.5°C stands at approximately 150 billion tonnes. Lead author Pierre Friedlingstein (University of Exeter) cautions the decline is not durable — the companion Nature Climate Change paper is titled 'A further acceleration of clean energy is needed for global CO₂ emissions to peak and decline.' Whether 2026 is peak fossil emissions remains open.

items.headline: COP31 Day 2 (Energy Day): EU Declares New Finance Pledges “Dead in the Water”; Turkey’s Electrification Pledge Draws Clean-Energy Friction; Fossil-Fuel Roadmap Relaunches for Third Time
items.summary: COP31's Day 2, designated Energy Day, opened with an immediate finance confrontation. A senior EU climate official declared that developing-country demands for new developed-world financing pledges beyond the NCQG framework are 'dead in the water,' antagonising the G77 and India bloc. Turkey's signature action-agenda ask — raising electricity's share of global final energy from ~20% to 35% by 2035 — drew EU pushback because the pledge lacks a 'clean electricity' qualifier, potentially counting new natural gas capacity toward the target. The COP28-era fossil-fuel transition roadmap was officially relaunched for the third time, with Oil Change International noting it still lacks supply-side production phase-out language. The overall climate work programme (covering mitigation and adaptation implementation) was added to the official agenda after procedural friction on Day 1. UNFCCC estimates 90,000–100,000 participants in Antalya.

items.headline: 2026 US Midterm Elections: Democrats Win Both Chambers; Climate Cabinet Claims 90%+ Win Rate; Abbott Loses Texas; IRA Residential Credits Still Ended by ‘One Big Beautiful Bill’
items.summary: The November 3, 2026 US midterm elections produced a historic 'blue wave,' with Democrats winning control of both the House and Senate. Climate Cabinet reported a 90%+ win rate on 95 targeted climate races. Texas Governor Greg Abbott lost re-election to Democrat Gina Hinojosa in the race's highest-profile result. A Democratic Congress can issue subpoenas to investigate the Trump administration's redirection of IRA and Department of Energy funding — several legislators have alleged those redirections violate the Impoundment Control Act. However, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, which ended the residential Investment Tax Credit for rooftop solar, the battery storage credit, and the new EV credit, remains law; restoring those credits requires passing new legislation that would face a presidential veto, seen as unachievable before 2028. Voters in various jurisdictions passed 38 ballot measures restricting data center construction, reflecting backlash against the AI-driven electricity demand surge. Solar and wind continued to account for 95% of new US generating capacity added in Q1 2026 at the utility scale.

items.headline: COP31 World Leaders Summit Set for Tomorrow November 11–12: Lula Confirmed; Erdoğan Chairs; Guterres Urges ‘Get Serious’; Few New Binding Pledges Expected
items.summary: The COP31 World Leaders Summit convenes tomorrow and Wednesday (November 11–12), with Brazil's President Lula confirmed to attend and Turkey's President Erdoğan chairing the opening plenary. UN Secretary-General António Guterres urged assembled leaders to 'get serious,' noting that current globally-agreed NDCs put the world on a pathway to nearly 3°C of warming. Diplomatic reporting suggests few if any new binding commitments will emerge: the summit agenda focuses on creating the 'just transition mechanism' agreed at COP29, discussing adaptation metrics, and Turkey's non-binding action pledges on AI-for-climate and waste management. The US Trump administration is not attending formal UNFCCC proceedings for the second year in a row. Negotiators are expected to begin drafting elements of a cover decision text in parallel with the leaders' segment.

major_events.name: Typhoon Samuel (Cempaka) — Category 2 Heading ENE; Philippines, China and Vietnam Now Clear
major_events.status: Recurved, moving away from all land — As of the 9 AM JST November 10 advisory, Typhoon Samuel is at approximately 25°N 138°E, moving east-northeast at 15 mph with 110 mph sustained winds (Category 2 equivalent); it exited the Philippine Area of Responsibility Monday evening as forecast, with no tropical cyclone wind signals issued for the Philippines; its 5-day track projects it into open ocean northeast of Japan, away from China, Vietnam and all major landmasses; storm is forecast to gradually weaken over cooler waters
major_events.impact: A significant de-escalation from yesterday's uncertainty. The Philippines, China and Vietnam face no threat from Samuel. The enhanced northeast monsoon (amihan) effect on Luzon is now diminishing as the storm pulls away. No storm watches or warnings are in effect for any populated area. JTWC projects gradual weakening over the next 5 days over progressively cooler open-ocean waters northeast of Japan.

major_events.name: Florida St. Johns River Flooding — Cocoa Gauge AT Major Flood Stage; Water Entering Homes; Sanford, DeLand, Geneva Rising
major_events.status: Escalating; peak at northern gauges still days away — NWS Melbourne issued new flood warnings at 8:04 PM EST November 9 confirming the Cocoa gauge is now AT major flood stage (17.0 ft); water is entering homes in the Lake Poinsett area, Rockledge’s Silver Pines subdivision, and Cocoa’s Shakespeare Park; Geneva is above moderate stage and forecast to approach major stage next weekend; Sanford rises above minor stage Thursday; DeLand rises above minor stage later this week; Governor’s 14-county declaration in force
major_events.impact: An escalation in severity: at Cocoa, floodwaters have now entered residential structures for the first time in this event. The slow-drain trajectory of the St. Johns River system means peaks at northern gauges (Sanford, DeLand, Astor) remain days to over a week away. No significant new rainfall is forecast; nevertheless, the existing runoff pulse continues northward through the basin. Two fatalities confirmed statewide from the broader flood event that began with the November 1–2 extreme rainfall.

major_events.name: Tropical Storm Pena (Central Pacific) — First November CPac Tropical Storm Since 1982; Strengthening; No Land Threat
major_events.status: Active, strengthening over open ocean — Tropical Storm Pena formed November 6 approximately 650 miles southeast of the Big Island of Hawaii — the first November tropical storm to form in the Central Pacific since 1982, the previous Super El Niño year — and is forecast to gradually strengthen over warm sea surface temperatures; some models project hurricane-intensity strengthening; none show a land threat to Hawaii or any inhabited island; Central Pacific Hurricane Center advisories continuing
major_events.impact: Pena poses no threat to any populated area. Its significance is meteorological: a November formation in the Central Pacific is an extremely rare event, occurring only under Super El Niño conditions. The storm reflects the historically warm Central Pacific SSTs in the current El Niño cycle. The Central Pacific season has already been active, with major Hurricane Lowell making landfall earlier in 2026. Pena may become the season's 14th hurricane.

weather.overview_html: Typhoon Samuel (Cempaka) has recurved to Category 2 heading east-northeast, fully clearing the Philippine Area of Responsibility with no land threat to China, Vietnam or the Philippines — a significant de-escalation from yesterday. Florida’s St. Johns River flooding has intensified: NWS Melbourne confirmed the Cocoa gauge is now AT major flood stage (17.0 ft) with water entering homes; Sanford rises above minor flood stage Thursday and DeLand later this week. Tropical Storm Pena formed November 6 in the Central Pacific — the first November CPac tropical storm since the 1982 Super El Niño — a stark El Niño signal consistent with the historically warm SSTs now confirmed by the NOAA ENSO advisory. Early-November flooding in the US Southwest set more than ten all-time gauge records and raised Lake Powell 20 feet from its September record low, partially easing the Colorado River drought crisis.

items.headline: Typhoon Samuel (Cempaka) Update: Category 2, 25°N 138°E, Heading ENE at 15 mph; Exited Philippine PAR; No Land Threat to Philippines, China or Vietnam
items.summary: As of the 9 AM JST November 10 advisory, Typhoon Samuel (international name Cempaka) is at approximately 25°N 138°E, moving east-northeast at 15 mph with 110 mph maximum sustained winds and 130 mph gusts — a Category 2 equivalent on the Saffir-Simpson scale. The storm exited the Philippine Area of Responsibility Monday evening, as forecast, without issuing any tropical cyclone wind signals for the Philippines. JTWC projects the storm to track northeast into open ocean over progressively cooler waters and gradually weaken over the next 5 days. No tropical cyclone watches or warnings are in effect for any populated area. The Philippines, China, Vietnam and Taiwan face no threat from Samuel.

items.source: Fox Weather / NHC Central Pacific Hurricane Center
items.headline: Tropical Storm Pena Forms in Central Pacific — First November Central Pacific Tropical Storm Since 1982 Super El Niño Year; Possible Hurricane Strengthening; No Threat to Hawaii
items.summary: Tropical Storm Pena formed November 6 approximately 650 miles southeast of the Big Island of Hawaii, becoming the first November tropical storm to form in the Central Pacific since 1982 — which was also a Super El Niño year. As of the November 7 advisory, Pena had 50 mph winds and was moving west at 13 mph. Forecasters expect gradual strengthening over favorable warm sea surface temperatures associated with the current strong El Niño event; some models project hurricane-intensity development. No forecast track shows a threat to Hawaii or any inhabited island. The Central Pacific Hurricane Center continues issuing advisories. The formation is a compelling indicator of El Niño's influence on Pacific tropical cyclone activity, deepening an already historically active Central Pacific season.

items.headline: St. Johns River Flooding Escalates: Cocoa Gauge AT Major Flood Stage (17.0 ft); Water in Homes in Rockledge and Cocoa; Sanford Rises Thursday; DeLand, Geneva to Follow
items.summary: New NWS Melbourne flood warnings issued at 8:04 PM EST on November 9 confirm the Cocoa gauge has reached 17.0 feet — major flood stage — with water now actively entering residential structures in the Lake Poinsett area and low-lying neighborhoods in Rockledge's Silver Pines subdivision and Cocoa's Shakespeare Park. Upstream, the Geneva gauge is above moderate flood stage and forecast to approach major flood stage by next weekend. The Sanford gauge is forecast to rise above minor flood stage Thursday. The DeLand gauge is expected to exceed minor flood stage later this week. The flooding propagates northward through the St. Johns slow-drain river system following the extreme November 1–2 rainfall event in Brevard County (20+ inches in under 24 hours). No significant new rainfall is in the forecast, yet peak levels at northern gauges remain days to over a week away.

items.headline: SW US Early-November Flooding Sets 10+ All-Time Gauge Records; Lake Powell Rises 20 Feet from September Record Low; US Drought Coverage Falls to Lowest Since January
items.summary: Atmospheric river-driven storms in the first week of November brought historic flooding to the US Southwest, setting all-time records at more than ten stream gauges across Arizona, New Mexico and Colorado. Hundreds of people were ordered to evacuate from low-lying areas. The same precipitation delivered rare relief for regional water management: Lake Powell, which fell to a record low in September 2026 (3,517.24 ft, below the prior 2023 record), has risen approximately 20 feet from that low. US drought coverage fell to approximately 44% of the contiguous US as of November 3 — its lowest extent since January 2026. The AP notes the flooding is consistent with the pattern of extreme precipitation events clustering under the current strong El Niño — the same system driving the November 1–2 Florida extreme rainfall, the Central Pacific tropical storm activity, and the Southeast Asian peat-fire drought.

renewables.overview_html: The Democratic sweep of both congressional chambers in the November 3 US midterms reshapes the domestic clean-energy oversight landscape: a Democratic Congress can investigate IRA fund redirections, though the One Big Beautiful Bill’s gutting of residential solar, battery and EV credits remains law and faces an uncertain path while utility-scale deployment continues strong (solar and wind supplied 95% of new US generating capacity in Q1 2026). In European project finance, Rezolv Energy closed €367 million in project financing for its 292.5 MW Dunarea East wind farm in Romania, backed by EBRD participation and an EU InvestEU guarantee. In the US, Crayhill-backed Sunraycer Renewables acquired 325 MWac of MISO solar projects in Illinois and Missouri from Apricus Energy, adding to its ~3 GW US pipeline.

items.headline: 2026 US Midterms: Democrat Congress May Restore Climate Oversight and Investigate IRA Redirection; Utility-Scale Solar and Wind Continue at 95% of New US Generating Capacity
items.summary: The 2026 US midterm elections, with Democrats winning control of both the House and Senate, change the oversight and legislative landscape for clean energy in several material ways. A Democratic-controlled Congress can issue subpoenas to investigate the Trump administration's reallocation of IRA program funds — a move several legislators have alleged violates the Impoundment Control Act. Congressional committees with clean-energy jurisdiction are expected to hold public hearings in early 2027. However, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act — which ended the residential Investment Tax Credit for rooftop solar, the residential battery storage credit, and the new EV credit — remains law; restoring those credits requires new legislation that would face a presidential veto, seen as infeasible before 2028. Solar and wind continue to account for approximately 95% of new US generating capacity added at the utility scale in Q1 2026, with solar alone at 78%. Interconnection queues, permitting delays and transmission shortages remain the principal structural constraints on further acceleration.

items.headline: Rezolv Energy Closes €367 Million Project Finance for 292.5 MW Dunarea East Wind Farm, Romania; EBRD, Six Commercial Banks, InvestEU First-Loss Guarantee; COD 2029
items.summary: Rezolv Energy closed project financing of up to €367 million for the Dunarea East wind farm (292.5 MW) in Constanța County, Romania — one of the largest wind project financings in Southeast Europe. The lending syndicate comprises six commercial banks (Société Générale, Erste Group, Raiffeisen Bank International, Raiffeisen Bank S.A., Mizuho, and Raiffeisenlandesbank Niederösterreich-Wien) plus a €31.9 million senior loan from the EBRD. A €7.6 million first-loss guarantee from the EU's InvestEU programme backstops the EBRD tranche. Danish export credit agency EIFO also backs the facility. Revenue is underpinned by a Contract for Difference covering 211 MW won at Romania's 2025 CfD auction, plus a corporate PPA with Ahold Delhaize. Commercial operation is expected in early 2029. When commissioned, Rezolv's total Romanian onshore wind portfolio will exceed 760 MW; total senior debt raised for Romanian projects now stands at approximately €1.55 billion.

items.headline: Sunraycer Renewables Acquires 325 MWac Gem City (IL) + Mighty Mississippi (MO) Solar Projects from Apricus Energy; MISO Expansion; $92 M Local Tax Revenue; Construction 2028
items.summary: Crayhill Capital-backed Sunraycer Renewables has acquired two utility-scale solar PV projects totalling 325 MWac from Apricus Energy (a joint venture of NOVI Energy and Osaka Gas USA): the 175 MWac Gem City project in Adams County, Illinois, and the 150 MWac Mighty Mississippi project in New Madrid County, Missouri. The acquisition expands Sunraycer's footprint in the MISO electricity market into two new states. Financial terms were not disclosed. Construction is scheduled to begin in early 2028 with commercial operations expected in 2029. The projects are expected to support 560 construction jobs and generate approximately $92 million in local tax revenue over their operating lives. Safe-harbored equipment may support eligibility for federal clean-energy tax credits under the IRA's ITC provisions. Sunraycer now holds approximately 3 GW of solar and battery projects across its development-to-operational pipeline in the United States.

science.overview_html: The 2026 Global Carbon Budget publication in Earth System Science Data is the week’s headline science release, arriving in time for COP31: fossil CO2 falls 0.4% to 38.2 Gt, atmospheric concentration hits 427.7 ppm, and the companion Nature Climate Change paper from Pierre Friedlingstein and colleagues warns that the decline is not durable without a further acceleration of clean energy deployment. On the AI weather frontier, ECMWF’s AI Weather Quest is completing its first full competitive year ahead of the Extended Phase launching November 12; Chinese firm Envision claimed its physics–AI hybrid Tianji model topped the latest leaderboard period (unconfirmed by ECMWF), while earlier in the year MicroEnsemble won the DJF 2025/26 period — illustrating how the best sub-seasonal ML systems are now competitive with, though not yet clearly superior to, dynamical ensemble systems on operational probabilistic metrics.

items.source: Global Carbon Project / ESSD & Nature Climate Change
items.headline: Global Carbon Budget 2026 Published: Fossil CO<sub>2</sub> −0.4% to 38.2 Gt; Total CO<sub>2</sub> Record 43.3 Gt; 427.7 ppm; ~150 Gt Remaining to 1.5°C; Decline Attributed Partly to Iran War Oil Shock
items.meta: Friedlingstein et al. · Earth System Science Data 2026 (preprint essd-2026-895); companion paper in Nature Climate Change, November 2026
items.summary: The 2026 Global Carbon Budget, published November 10 in Earth System Science Data alongside a companion paper in Nature Climate Change, projects global fossil CO₂ emissions to fall 0.4% to 38.2 billion tonnes in 2026 — the first annual decline since 2020. The decline is partly structural (solar/wind displacement of thermal generation) and partly geopolitical (Iran conflict oil shock: oil −1.9%; China oil use −5%). By fuel: coal +0.6%, gas −0.3%. By emitter: China overall −0.9%, India +4.4% (coal growth). Land-use change emissions surge to 5.1 billion tonnes (driven by El Niño-amplified peat fires in Southeast Asia), pushing total CO₂ to a record 43.3 billion tonnes. Atmospheric CO₂ concentration: 427.7 ppm, 54% above pre-industrial. Remaining carbon budget for 1.5°C: approximately 150 billion tonnes. Lead author Pierre Friedlingstein (Exeter) cautions the decline is not durable; the companion Nature Climate Change paper explicitly asks whether 2026 is peak fossil emissions and concludes the evidence is insufficient to claim so, emphasising that clean energy growth is not yet fast enough for a durable annual decline.

items.headline: ECMWF AI Weather Quest: Year 1 Completing — MicroEnsemble Wins DJF Period; Chinese Envision Tianji Claims Latest Period Top; Extended Phase Begins November 12
items.summary: ECMWF's AI Weather Quest — a benchmark competition for sub-seasonal ML weather forecasting running in real-time against the operational IFS ensemble — is completing its first full competitive year (SON 2025 through JJA 2026 periods) ahead of the Extended Phase launching November 12, 2026. MicroEnsemble was named the winner for the DJF 2025/26 (December–February) period. Chinese green-energy technology company Envision claimed in an October 30 press release that its Tianji weather foundation model, which uses a physics–AI hybrid architecture, topped the most recent period's leaderboard; ECMWF has not independently published updated aggregate standings. The competition's Year 1 results broadly align with the emerging consensus: ML systems achieve competitive probabilistic skill with dynamical ensembles at sub-seasonal lead times but have not yet demonstrated consistent, clear outperformance across metrics and seasons in an operational regime.

items.title: LiCuSpace Raises ~€3 Million Led by IBG-Fonds Sachsen-Anhalt for Atmospheric LiDAR Platform Targeting Wind Energy and Maritime Shipping; Relocates HQ to Magdeburg
items.body_html: German atmospheric lidar startup LiCuSpace has secured approximately €3 million in funding led by IBG-Fonds Sachsen-Anhalt, with existing shareholders including the NORIS Group retaining their stakes. The company’s flagship product, the LidarCUBE, measures wind speed and atmospheric temperature up to approximately 100 km altitude using laser-based remote sensing; its FullSky software platform manages data processing and visualisation. Primary commercial applications target wind energy (turbine siting, operational optimisation, wake characterisation) and maritime shipping (atmospheric characterisation for route optimisation). As part of the financing, LiCuSpace has relocated its corporate headquarters to Magdeburg, Saxony-Anhalt. The round positions the company to commercialise atmospheric lidar applications as AI-driven numerical weather prediction and wind resource assessment demand higher-resolution vertical wind profiles.

items.title: NextEra–Dominion $67 Billion Merger: Evidentiary Hearing November 17; Companies Now Agree to 101 of 117 SCC-Proposed Conditions; Clean Virginia Discovery Motion Pending
items.body_html: The Virginia State Corporation Commission evidentiary hearing on the proposed $67 billion NextEra Energy acquisition of Dominion Energy is set for November 17, with a final SCC decision expected January 11, 2027. New filings this week show NextEra and Dominion have agreed to 101 of the 117 proposed conditions and safeguards, accepting most consumer protection and financial ring-fencing measures while rejecting or modifying certain independent-oversight provisions. Clean Virginia’s motion to compel additional document discovery remains pending. The combined company would serve roughly 10 million utility customers across Virginia, Florida, North Carolina and South Carolina, and would reshape regulated-utility ownership of approximately 7 GW of Dominion’s Virginia offshore wind pipeline. If approved, the deal would be the largest regulated-utility merger since FirstEnergy’s 2000 acquisition.

items.title: Ørsted Q3 2026: DKK 28 Billion EBITDA Guidance On Track; Investment Outlook Lowered; US Permit Reconsideration Cited as Principal Drag; New Congressional Meetings Sought
items.body_html: Ørsted confirmed at Q3 2026 earnings that it remains on track for full-year EBITDA guidance of approximately DKK 28 billion (€3.75 billion), but the company lowered its annual investment outlook, reflecting extended timelines for US offshore wind projects under the Trump administration’s permit reconsideration actions. Ørsted reiterated that recovery in the US offshore wind investment environment is contingent on regulatory clarity, and said it has sought meetings with incoming congressional committee leadership following the November 3 Democratic midterm victories. The company’s Revolution Wind (704 MW, Rhode Island/Connecticut) remains under active construction while permit reconsideration proceedings are ongoing, and the broader US pipeline remains on hold pending policy resolution.
